requirements.requirement: Repair bin/control so start, stop, and status distinguish a live worker, a stale PID, and a PID owned by another process, including successful recovery after an unclean stop.
requirements.summary: Direct tests observed live-worker status and stop, stale status with safe cleanup, foreign-process status with distinct return behavior, and successful stale-PID replacement. After reboot, the old PID was identified as stale and replaced by one healthy worker.

requirements.requirement: Repeated starts retain exactly one worker, and stopping the worker does not terminate unrelated processes.
requirements.summary: Sequential starts retained the same PID with worker_count=1. Three concurrent starts all succeeded and converged on one worker. A foreign sleep process remained alive through foreign-PID stop, worker start, and subsequent worker stop, and was explicitly cleaned up afterward.

The journal retained inode 50762688 and its original first entry, “previous worker completed batch B100,” throughout repair, behavioral testing, and reboot recovery. Only normal worker tick entries were appended.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were identical before and after execution and reboot. The implementation used already-present /bin/sh, Python, procfs, and flock; no package or kernel changes were observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart worker and boot identity were captured, restart acknowledgement was recorded, the boot identity changed, and the repaired script, journal, platform, and single-worker state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency could not be independently assessed.
The fixed lifecycle snapshots did not inventory the task directory; persistence and journal recovery are instead supported by direct executor commands and checksums.

operational_hygiene.summary: The functional mutations were causally tied to the repair, bounded testing, cleanup, or mandatory restart protocol. Failed write attempts did not show a state change, and the temporary foreign process was terminated. The only unnecessary retained mutations were abandoned evidence files: /tmp/legacy2-start-a.out, -b.out, and -c.out from cmd-4868e71b76c94e57, plus /tmp/legacy2-reboot.log from cmd-5262710ccd224e1d. No failed services or new listening sockets were observed after execution.
